tagline: An open-source PyTorch pipeline for training a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch

scenes.narration: Day 51: minimind, an open source pipeline that trains a 64M parameter LLM from scratch, run on CPU.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Pure PyTorch: pretrain, SFT, LoRA, DPO, GRPO, CISPO
Claims a 2-hour training run on one GPU
scenes.narration: minimind implements the full training pipeline, tokenizer, pretraining, fine tuning, and reinforcement learning, in pure PyTorch, with no high level wrappers.

steps.narration: We sliced the official dataset down to under half a percent, and ran the stock pretrain script on four CPU cores, no GPU.
The SFT script loaded that checkpoint and kept training on a small set of chat examples, still on CPU only.
We then generated from both checkpoints with the same seed, comparing raw text continuation against fine-tuned chat replies.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Pretrain loss over 1,672 steps on CPU. SFT then took it from 4.99 to 3.51.
lines: both    still wrong on hard facts
scenes.narration: Pretrain loss dropped from seven point four to four point one over one thousand six hundred steps. After SFT, the model gave a coherent self-introduction, but factual questions stayed incoherent.
Full logs and code are on GitHub, Apache-2.0 licensed. Write-up linked below.
